text:
Sara Liu: :wave: Hey — quick question for fellow new-hires: what's the practical rulebook for where to post things during week 1? e.g., setup/install help, infra access requests, product questions, status updates. Also, any tips for muting noisy bots but still keeping critical alerts? Trying not to blow up everyone's feed while I sort my laptop.

Mike Patel: For installs and access, #help is the fastest. If it's eng-specific infra (deploy keys, VPN), use #eng-infra. Product or roadmap q's -> #product. Small config questions — start a thread in the team channel so it doesn't become a new top-level message.

Katie O'Neill: Rule of thumb I give new folks: 1) If multiple teams need to see it -> post in the relevant channel. 2) If it's just you + 1 person -> DM. 3) If it grows into a back-and-forth -> move into a thread (click "reply in thread"). For outages/pagers, always use the @oncall flow in #eng-oncall or whichever channel is listed in the oncall rota.

Ben R.: For bot noise: don't mute channels blindly — instead mute the specific app notifications you don't care about. Click channel name > Integrations or View apps -> find the bot -> adjust settings. Also you can set desktop/mobile keywords so you only get alerts for things tagged with your name or "urgent".

DevEx Bot: Hi Sara! Welcome :tada: — quick onboarding links you might find helpful: https://intranet.redwood/handbook/onboarding and https://intranet.redwood/devex/bots. To subscribe/unsubscribe to our onboarding digest: run the slash command below in any channel you have access to:
```
/onboard subscribe
/onboard unsubscribe
```
To silence DeployBot in a channel (recommended: mute non-critical notifications): open the channel > Integrations > DeployBot > toggle "only notify on failures".

OnboardBot: Welcome Sara! If you're waiting on access, ping @Ben R. or post in #help with the template: "name / team / resource requested / urgency" — that'll speed things up. If you want a buddy, reply here and I'll assign someone.

Alex Gomez: TL;DR cheat sheet for what to post where:
- Startups/ops/quick logistical Qs -> #new-hires or #help
- Infra/deploy/config -> #eng-infra
- Runtime/perf/serving-specific -> #eng-runtime
- Product/feature discussions -> #product
- Urgent site impact -> @oncall in #eng-oncall AND a thread in #incidents
- Everyday FYIs -> thread in your team channel (keeps the main channel readable)

Alex Gomez: Quick examples you can copy: 
```
In #eng-infra (new thread): "Alex G: Trying to add my SSH key to ops-hosts, getting 'permission denied' — anyone seen this?"
DM to person: "Hey Katie — do you have a minute for a quick question about the deploy role?"
```

Sara Liu: Amazing, this helps a lot — thanks everyone! I'll post access requests to #help, infra stuff to #eng-infra, and thread by default. :thumbsup: If someone wants to be my buddy that'd be awesome.

Mike Patel: I'll volunteer to be a buddy — sent you a DM, Sara. :slightly_smiling_face:

Katie O'Neill: Also pro tip: add channel-specific notification preferences (three dots on desktop) and mark channels "mute" if you only want to check them manually. Saves sanity.

Sara Liu: Got it. Thanks again :heart:
